items.quote: The solidus and liquidus temperature were determined by DSC using the method described in a previous study.[90] First, the chamber was evacuated to 2 9 10-4 Pa, then backfilled with Ar. To remove traces of oxygen in the gas atmosphere, Ti chips were placed near the sample holder.

items.method: inductively coupled plasma atomic emission spectroscopy
items.quote: The chemical composition of the phosphorus of the alloys was analyzed using inductively coupled plasma atomic emission spectroscopy and is listed in Table 1.
The surfaces of the samples were mirror-polished and their chemical compositions analyzed using EPMA.

An alumina sample container was used for the measurement. The same sample was repeatedly melted at different heating rates. The heating rate for the first melting was 15  C/min; however, this curve was not used for the evaluation because the change in the sample shape from angular to droplet form during melting affected the shape of the DSC curve. For the second, third, and fourth cycles, the heating rates were varied to 4, 8, and 12  C/min., respectively.

The alloys were melted under an Ar gas atmosphere using an alumina crucible. After the melting, the molten alloy was cast into a metal mold to produce ingots with a diameter of 10 mm. Specimens weighing approximately 200 mg were cut from the ingots for DSC measurements. The chemical composition of the phosphorus of the alloys was analyzed using inductively coupled plasma atomic emission spectroscopy and is listed in Table 1.
items.synthesis: The alloys were melted under an Ar gas atmosphere using an alumina crucible. After the melting, the molten alloy was cast into a metal mold to produce ingots with a diameter of 10 mm.

items.atmosphere_or_container: sealed in a quartz capsule filled with an Ar gas after evacuation
items.quote: A small specimen was cut from the Cu-4 alloy ingot, sealed in a quartz capsule filled with an Ar gas after evacuation, and annealed at 550 and 600  C for 168 h. After equilibration, the samples were quenched into ice water.
